notes:
Changes to know about: uninstall is now a ccam command, so new accounts cannot take that name. An account already called uninstall keeps working, but ccam uninstall now runs the new command: start that account with ccam run uninstall, its number or its shortcut, or rename it with ccam rename uninstall <new-name>. Nothing else behaves differently.

New

  • ccam uninstall removes ccam in one step: every account as ccam remove does (logged out first), the shortcut commands, ~/.config/ccam, ~/.local/share/ccam, ~/.local/state/ccam and the ccam binary. It lists what goes and asks first, and ccam --dry-run uninstall only lists it. An imported ~/.claude stays for plain claude, with a copy of what it shared in its groups and the status line it had before ccam. A .deb install is left to apt (sudo apt remove ccam); on Windows it prints the Remove-Item command for ccam.exe

Changes to know about: nothing behaves differently. Some messages are reworded to match the rewritten English docs on ccam.dev, so a script that matches ccam's exact output text may need updating. When ccam update cannot replace the binary itself, it now suggests the install script at https://ccam.dev/install.sh (or install.ps1 on Windows) instead of the GitHub raw address. The Claude Code plugin is now 0.3.1, with the same wording in its command, hook and skill descriptions.

Fixed

  • Plainer wording in the messages of ccam next, the relay, auto_switch, ccam mcp, groups, ccam doctor and the lock, matching the docs that quote them
  • ccam update and the READMEs give the install commands from ccam.dev

Changes to know about: the dashboard (ccam in a terminal) now says at the end of its tab line whether auto_switch is on, on every tab. Windows, which ignores auto_switch, shows nothing there.

New

  • The dashboard's tab line says whether auto_switch is on

Changes to know about: ccusage is now a ccam command, so an account named ccusage starts with ccam run ccusage (ccam doctor says so). When ccusage is not installed, ccam ccusage runs it with bun x ccusage or npx ccusage@latest, which fetch it from npm.

New

  • ccam ccusage runs ccusage's token and cost reports over the conversations of every account, or of the accounts -a names

Changes to know about: auto_switch = true in config.toml (Linux and macOS; off by default and experimental) lets ccam move an interactive session that Claude Code stops at a usage limit to another of your accounts with room, and sends one fixed message in your place so the conversation goes on. It needs the ccam plugin and Claude Code 2.1.214 or later, and it moves work only between seats of one Team or Enterprise organization or between personal plans. Moving between seats may violate Anthropic's terms, and for personal plans the terms do not settle it: read the conditions and Anthropic's terms before you turn it on.

New

  • With auto_switch = true (Linux and macOS), a session that Claude Code stops at its 5-hour, weekly, Opus or Sonnet limit continues as another account with room, among seats of the same Team or Enterprise organization or among personal plans
  • ccam next --continue --brief starts a new conversation from ccam's summary of the old one instead of resuming all of it
  • The dashboard's Agents tab lists every account's background and open sessions; Enter attaches to one and x stops it
  • ccam doctor checks what auto_switch needs: the ccam plugin and Claude Code 2.1.214 or later
  • At a usage limit, the notification says so when you have no other account that may carry the conversation on

Fixed

  • ccam pick --json no longer calls the account it picked the least used when it passed over one picked a moment ago
  • The dashboard's Folders tab no longer runs past its column on folder names with double-width characters

Changes to know about: old /ccam:switch notes (state/handoff/<account>.json) are not read any more; a line in config.toml that ccam does not read is reported, and commands that save the config refuse until it is fixed; --wait and --watch take their value after = (--wait=2h). Automatic choice (next --auto, pick, --fallback, the dashboard's n) also moves work between seats of one Team or Enterprise organization, which may violate Anthropic's terms: see the FAQ.

New

  • When Claude Code stops at a usage limit, ccam records the full window and treats the account as full until Claude Code's reported reset, in next --auto, pick, --fallback, the dashboard and ccam usage
  • /ccam:switch under relay = true keeps the session's flags, permission mode and effort level, never asks the shared-history question during the hop, and does not hop after you end Claude Code yourself
  • ccam ext, ccam doctor, ccam mcp list and next --continue show MCP servers only one account has, local-scope servers, servers still only in ~/.claude.json, and which account still has to sign in to which MCP server
  • Leaving MCP sharing keeps the group's servers in the account's .claude.json, and a group change that stops halfway is finished by ccam doctor --fix
  • ccam remove logs the account out before it moves the folder to the trash, and ccam logout says first which MCP sign-ins go with the login
  • Checks for a running account also see Claude Code sessions ccam did not start, such as plain claude and background jobs

Fixed

  • With mcp_strategy = "sync", ccam never overwrites or deletes an MCP server the account added itself
  • ccam usage --refresh no longer loses a renewed login on a timeout or Ctrl+C, and keeps what Claude Code wrote meanwhile
  • ccam migrate no longer copies MCP sign-ins, which made the copies log each other out
  • On macOS, ccam rename keeps the account's folder, so its Keychain login stays
  • Two sessions of one account no longer overwrite each other's /ccam:switch note
  • /ccam:switch promises that ccam carries the conversation on only in a session its own relay started; any other session is told to /exit and run ccam next --continue
  • A Claude Code that has ended but that nothing has reaped (as under a container's PID 1) no longer counts as running, so rename, remove and group changes no longer refuse with "work is running"
  • ccam next --continue resumes the right conversation and skips sessions without one
  • -p workers whose input is /dev/null are no longer cancelled by the shared-history question
  • Removing an account imported in place gives the folder its own files back and leaves nothing linked into ccam's groups
  • A group change, a copy back or a merge that stops halfway no longer leaves a missing folder or a lost file
  • --fallback no longer hangs on an open pipe, keeps to its --wait limit, passes a run ended by a signal through, and never retries another folder of the Claude account that hit its limit
  • The dashboard no longer crashes on the Health tab, and doctor --fix says when it replaces an account's own file with the group's copy
  • Windows: arguments to an npm claude.cmd are quoted safely for cmd.exe, Ctrl+C after a relay hop no longer ends ccam, hard-link shortcuts are relinked after an update, and install.ps1 keeps %VARIABLES% in the user PATH

Fixed

  • ccam ext no longer reports skills/synced as a skill without SKILL.md

New

  • The dashboard recommends a newer ccam release, and U installs it

New

  • F in the dashboard's Health tab repairs only the selected box; F repairs everything

New

  • Usage bars for the 5-hour, weekly and Fable limits, and a box per account in ccam doctor and the Health tab

Fixed

  • ccam doctor --fix leaves out the "makes it" hint on a link it makes

Fixed

  • ccam doctor says how a missing share link gets made, and ccam hook --help is accurate

New

  • The ccam plugin notifies at a usage limit and adds /ccam:switch
  • Groups, a full-screen dashboard, and carrying a conversation on to another account at a usage limit

New

  • Claude Code plugin for ccam (/plugin install ccam --marketplace jhyunwoo/ccam)
  • ccam pick, API key accounts, ccam ext, and choice rules with --wait and exit code 75

New

  • Windows support, ccam folder, and ccam --fallback for -p runs

Fixed

  • Refresh tokens at platform.claude.com, as Claude Code does

Fixed

  • Remote Control starts with shared MCP servers and asks to copy them

New

  • Show a * for each character typed during login
  • ccam migrate picks items from a checklist and copies MCP sign-ins
  • Finish a sign-in on a remote machine from the pasted callback address

Fixed

  • Verify every command and fix review findings

New

  • ccam update replaces the binary with the latest release

New

  • Shortcuts are opt-in and named by the user
  • ccam migrate copies an existing Claude Code setup into the shared group

Fixed

  • --no-login help reads as text, not a flag argument
  • Rename help no longer says it updates shortcuts

New

  • All program output is English
  • Support macOS and other Linux distributions
  • Phase 6 import, completion, PGO, CI, packaging and docs
  • Phase 5 TUI picker, share toggles and add wizard
  • Phase 4.5 usage lookup, status line collector, next --auto
  • Phase 4 history lock and ccam next
  • Phase 3 MCP sharing (flag and sync strategies)
  • Phase 2 share engine, ccam share and doctor
  • Phase 1 skeleton, profiles, launcher and shims

Fixed

  • Say <name|number> everywhere, not <name|slot>
  • Finish interrupted share changes and keep plugins when joining a group
  • Track running sessions by PID + start time instead of inherited flocks
  • Address final review findings
